name: Holderness & Bourne
city: Armonk, New York (HQ; started in Manhattan's Flatiron, 2015-2018)
why_quiet: Tailoring-led golf basics with deliberately minimal branding: the founders say they 'made a strong effort to minimize any H&B branding'. Knitwear is the quiet-luxury core: 100% Scottish cashmere made in Scotland (The Buckley) and a merino-cashmere blend across the McDaid and Cunningham sweaters, cut in heathered neutrals (driftwood, gray, navy, spruce).

quote.text: You have to stand behind it if your name is on it, and we liked that responsibility.

facts.fact: Founded in 2015 by Alex Holderness and John Bourne, who met getting MBAs at Yale.
HQ was a one-room Flatiron (NYC) office 2015-2018; later moved to Armonk, New York.
Founders put their names on the label 'like the old tailoring houses in England'.
Brand says it deliberately minimizes H&B branding so the club or resort logo leads; per PGA.com they 'didn't like exhaustive branding or big logos'.
Winged Foot was the first club to stock them; now in 1,300+ golf shops per PGA.com (Feb 2024); GolfWRX (2022) said 90%+ of the US top-100 courses.
The Buckley crewneck is 100% Scottish cashmere, made in Scotland; McDaid and Cunningham are merino-cashmere blends.
Site runs a dedicated Merino-Cashmere Collection page.
